Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

A fix release for 0.17.0 on Android:

- **The game no longer hangs after the opening movie**: Android's movie player hangs when a movie that has run to its end is stopped, and 0.17.0's way of stopping the movie just before its end could miss on a slow phone, so the sample could hang at start-up after the logo's opening. The movie is now also stopped by the time since it started.
- **Saving no longer crashes the game**: 0.17.0's fix for the engine's shrinkCopy reading past the picture it shrinks (a save's thumbnail) didn't cover the last pixel, and a quick save could still crash the game. The thumbnail is shrunk from a copy with a column and two rows more now.
- kagex-release 0.17.1 downloads the 0.17.1 engines

Everything 0.17.0 added (settings laid out from one table, reading settings, the hero's name, the name box, on-screen indicators, movies with subtitles, the credits roll, writers' shorthands and `[vo]`, the Extras touches, Android manifest additions in kagex-release) is in [0.17.0's notes](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/releases/tag/0.17.0).

The sample game with Live2D (`kagex_sample_live2d_<platform>`, added to this release once it's out) holds Live2D's Cubism Core: by installing or playing it you agree not to copy the Cubism Core out of it, distribute it apart from the game, modify it, or reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble it. It uses sample data owned and copyrighted by Live2D Inc.

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.17.1/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tools aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tools, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release kagex-lipsync`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
